title: Request IDs and a safe 500 handler
problem: Complete app.py: every request gets a request ID (reused from a valid incoming X-Request-ID header, otherwise generated), every log record from the 'app' logger carries it, and any unhandled exception is logged with its traceback and answered with a generic 500 that contains only the request ID.
requirements: Middleware: if X-Request-ID matches VALID_ID, reuse it; otherwise use uuid.uuid4().hex
Store the ID in request_id_var and return it in the X-Request-ID response header
RequestIdFilter sets record.request_id from request_id_var on every record logged through log
An exception handler for Exception logs at ERROR with the traceback on the 'app' logger, with the method and path in the message
It returns status 500 with exactly {"detail": "Internal Server Error", "request_id": <id>} and the X-Request-ID header
Exception messages never reach the client; HTTPException responses (like the 404) stay unchanged
contract: app.py exposes app (FastAPI), log = logging.getLogger("app"), request_id_var (ContextVar[str]) and RequestIdFilter. Tests use TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False).
expectedBehavior: GET /orders/13 with X-Request-ID: trace-2 returns 500 {"detail": "Internal Server Error", "request_id": "trace-2"} with header X-Request-ID: trace-2, and the 'app' logger records an ERROR with exc_info and request_id 'trace-2'. GET /orders/1 without the header returns a fresh 32-character hex ID.
edgeCases: No incoming header: generate a new ID for every request
Incoming IDs with spaces, semicolons, empty or longer than 64 characters are replaced (they'd end up in your logs)
The 500 response for an unhandled exception doesn't pass back through @app.middleware, so the header must be set in the handler
HTTPException is handled by FastAPI's own handler and must not turn into a 500
hints: Conceptual: the request ID is per-request context, so it belongs in a ContextVar that the middleware sets and that both the logging filter and the error handler read. Unhandled exceptions are answered by the outermost layer, outside your middleware.

Specific: in the middleware, choose the ID, call request_id_var.set(...), await call_next(request), then set the header on the response. Register the handler with @app.exception_handler(Exception) and use log.exception(...) inside it.

Implementation: rid = incoming if VALID_ID.match(incoming) else uuid.uuid4().hex; in the filter record.request_id = request_id_var.get(); in the handler return JSONResponse(status_code=500, content={"detail": "Internal Server Error", "request_id": rid}, headers={"X-Request-ID": rid}).
evaluation: The handler's log message identifies the request (method and path) without logging secrets from the request
No str(exc) in the response body
